rules.message_template: No file uploaded
rules.trigger: req.file is undefined after multer processing (either nothing was attached, or fileFilter silently rejected it per UPLOAD-FILEFILTER-EXT-MIME).

rules.message_template: Invalid file format. Only modern Excel spreadsheets (.xlsx) are supported. Please convert your file to .xlsx and try again.
rules.trigger: path.extname(req.file.originalname) is not '.xlsx' (belt-and-braces re-check on disk after multer already accepted the upload).

rules.message_template: Invalid or missing record_type. Must be CASE, ARREST, KALANDRA, PCR_CALL, UIDB or MISSING.
rules.trigger: req.body.record_type (uppercased) is not one of VALID_RECORD_TYPES = ['ARREST','PCR_CALL','CASE','UIDB','MISSING','KALANDRA'].

rules.message_template: Operators (HC) cannot import legacy data
rules.trigger: req.user.role === 'HC' and is_legacy === true/'true' in the request body.
rules.config_driven: Hardcoded role/mode rule (D1/D2 mode rules), not config.

rules.message_template: Operators are restricted to importing for their assigned Station only
rules.trigger: req.user.role === 'HC' and body ps_id is present and differs from req.user.ps_id.
rules.config_driven: Hardcoded; ps_id is stamped from req.user, body value only checked/rejected, never trusted (P5.4).

rules.message_template: District officers may only import legacy (historical) data
rules.trigger: req.user.role === 'DISTRICT_OFFICER' and is_legacy is falsy.

rules.message_template: ps_id (the target police station) is required for a legacy import
rules.trigger: req.user.role === 'DISTRICT_OFFICER' and body ps_id is falsy.

rules.message_template: You can only import legacy data for a police station within your own district
rules.trigger: districtForPs(ps_id) resolves to no district, or to a district_id different from req.user.district_id.
rules.config_driven: Hardcoded; walks hierarchy_nodes.parent_id (DB data, not config) via districtForPs().

rules.message_template: Your role is not permitted to import data
rules.trigger: Default-deny else-branch: req.user.role is neither HC nor DISTRICT_OFFICER (should already be impossible -- router's allow('HC','DISTRICT_OFFICER') gates this endpoint -- but never falls through to treating an unrecognized role as authorized, P5.5).

rules.message_template: <raw multer MulterError.message>
rules.trigger: Uploaded file exceeds the hardcoded 10 MB multer limit; caught by the router-scoped MulterError middleware (line 109) and returned as HTTP 400 with multer's own (not police-domain-friendly) error text.

multer fileFilter: file extension is not '.xlsx' OR mimetype is not in the XLSX_ALLOWED_MIMES set -- silently calls cb(null, false), so req.file is simply absent downstream (no distinct error surfaces here; the controller's 'No file uploaded' check is what the operator actually sees).
rules.config_driven: Hardcoded XLSX_ALLOWED_MIMES set and '.xlsx' extension check in code, not config.

rules.trigger: HINT_ROW_PATTERNS regex matches >= max(2, ceil(0.4 * nonEmptyCellCount)) of a row's non-empty cells (looksLikeHintRow) -- used only to decide whether to skip ONE extra row (the Row-4 instruction row) after the detected header, at buildColumnMap:472-474. A hint row that doesn't match this pattern-density threshold is silently parsed as a data row instead (no error emitted either way).
rules.config_driven: HINT_ROW_PATTERNS is a hardcoded regex in code, not config.

rules.trigger: buildColumnMap scores rows 1-6 by how many cells match a known field_registry key (keyRow) vs. a known label/synonym (labelRow); if the best score is < 2 matches, that row is discarded entirely (keyRow/labelRow set to null) and every column in that role is unmapped. A file whose header uses labels/keys the scorer doesn't recognize can silently misdetect the header row or fail to map columns, with no diagnostic surfaced to the operator -- columns simply come through as null/unmapped and downstream required-field checks fire as if the operator left them blank.
rules.config_driven: Column matching runs against CASE_SYNONYMS/ARREST_SYNONYMS (hardcoded) plus field_registry label_en/label_hi (config/DB-driven) -- a mixed source.

rules.trigger: Exact condition: 'let isEmpty = true; row.eachCell({includeEmpty:false}, () => { isEmpty = false; }); if (isEmpty) return;' -- a row is dropped entirely, silently, with NO error/warning emitted and NO record of it ever existing, when ExcelJS reports it has zero cells with any value at all. This is looser than taxonomy.json's own E4 'ghost/trailing row' definition (<=2 non-blank cells): a row with 1 stray cell (e.g. a leftover date or copy-paste artifact) is NOT caught here and proceeds as a full data row with every other field blank, producing a cluster of REQUIRED_MISSING + RECORD_DATE_MISSING findings for that row -- exactly taxonomy.json's E4 class.
rules.config_driven: Hardcoded threshold (zero non-empty cells) in code; no field_registry/config involvement.

rules.message_template: Invalid template: main worksheet not found
rules.trigger: readWorkbook() (import.parse.js) returns null -- no parent worksheet could be resolved via findWorksheet()'s SHEET_ALIASES candidates, and the workbook.worksheets[0] fallback is also missing/absent.
rules.config_driven: Sheet-name candidates are hardcoded in SHEET_ALIASES (import.parse.js:349-376), not config.

rules.message_template: Reference '{parentVal}' in sheet '{sheetName}' does not exist in the parent sheet.
rules.trigger: A child-sheet row's parent-key cell (fir_no/linked_fir_dd_no/gd_no) is falsy OR parentIndex.resolve(parentVal) returns null (no unambiguous parent match by exact canonical key, or by FIR-sequence-alone when exactly one candidate parent is compatible). A BLANK key cell produces the exact same PARENT_KEY_MISSING error as an unmatched/garbled one -- the message interpolates the empty string as "Reference '' in sheet ..."; there is no separate 'blank key' code or message.
rules.scope: CASE (victim/act/accused/property sheets), ARREST/KALANDRA (act/person/property sheets), UIDB (act sheet)
rules.config_driven: parentKeyField comes from the hardcoded PARENT_KEY_FIELD map (import.parse.js:923); parent-key resolution logic (buildParentKeyIndex/canonKeyParts) is hardcoded, not config.

rules.message_template: "{label_en}" is required in sheet "{sheetName}".
rules.trigger: field.show_when evaluates true (or is absent) AND (field.required === true OR isRequired(field) via field.validation_rules.required) AND rowData[field.field_key] is null/undefined/''.
rules.scope: Every sheet of CASE/ARREST/KALANDRA/UIDB/MISSING (curated fields) and PCR_CALL (registry fields)
rules.config_driven: SPLIT SOURCE -- the central requiredness finding of this audit. For CASE/ARREST/KALANDRA/UIDB/MISSING, sheetFieldLists (validateBatch's fieldsList) is the CURATED list from import-fields.config.js (caseGeneralFields/arrestPersonFields/etc.) whose 'required: true/false' is a hand-authored boolean in that file, completely independent of field_registry.validation_rules.required -- the DB registry's requiredness is NEVER consulted for these types' required-check. These types' auto-appended (non-curated, registry-driven) template columns are not part of sheetFieldLists at all and so are NEVER required-checked, no matter what field_registry says (see Findings). Only PCR_CALL (the one generic/uncurated type) uses field_registry.validation_rules.required directly, via normalizeRegistryRow, which additionally applies IMPORT_OPTIONAL_REQUIRED_KEYS (registry-sync.util.js:83) to demote work_out_date/missing_fir_no/missing_fir_date to not-required for import specifically (interactive form still enforces them) -- import-only special-casing, but NOT is_legacy-aware: it applies identically to legacy and non-legacy batches.

rules.message_template: Duplicate {codeLabel} "{key}" found in sheet "{sheetName}".
rules.trigger: Two or more parent-sheet rows canonicalize (canonKey) to the same natural key (fir_no/linked_fir_dd_no/gd_no) -- parent sheet only, checked against the row's OWN key, never the child sheets.
rules.scope: CASE/ARREST/KALANDRA parent sheet (fir_no/linked_fir_dd_no); UIDB parent sheet (gd_no); not applied to MISSING/PCR_CALL (no parentKeyField)

rules.message_template: Act "{act}" is not in the acts list -- will be stored as free text.
rules.trigger: resolveAct() returns actId=null but otherActName is set (free-text fallback) -- informational only, in BOTH legacy and non-legacy modes (never escalated to ERROR), since record_offences.other_act_name is a schema-sanctioned free-text column.
rules.config_driven: Resolution against ref.acts (DB-loaded reference table) via records.normalize.js resolveAct.

rules.message_template: Section "{section}" (act "{act}") could not be matched to a known section.
rules.trigger: resolveSection() (case-insensitive exact match against ref.sections.section, optionally scoped to the act's act_cd(s)) returns no sectionId. A SECOND trigger for the SAME error_code exists at line 164: an offence row has a section but the act text failed to resolve to ANY act_id or otherActName at all (record_offences' CHECK would otherwise fail) -- same code, different message: "Section \"{section}\" has no associated act to resolve against."
rules.config_driven: Resolution against ref.sections (DB reference table, loaded via 'npm run load-ref'); matching is case-insensitive-exact only -- no fuzzy/substring/synonym matching.

rules.message_template: Major head "{major_head}" could not be matched.
rules.trigger: resolveMajorHead() (case-insensitive exact match against ref.major_heads.major_head) returns null for a non-empty offence-row major_head value.

rules.message_template: Minor head "{minor_head}" could not be matched.
rules.trigger: resolveMinorHead() (case-insensitive exact match against ref.minor_heads, scoped to major_head_code when known, with an unscoped fallback) returns null for a non-empty offence-row minor_head value.

rules.message_template: Local head "{local_head}" could not be matched.
rules.trigger: resolveLocalHead() (case-insensitive exact match against ref.local_heads.local_head) returns null for payload.data.local_head. Side effect: when isLegacy, payload.data.local_head_raw is set to the raw text (mutates the payload so the raw value survives to the write path via the storage:'extra' sibling field) -- no equivalent free-text fallback column exists for non-legacy imports, so a non-legacy unresolved local_head simply hard-errors with the text lost from the eventual record unless the operator re-validates with a corrected label.
rules.config_driven: ref.local_heads DB table; local_head_raw storage:'extra' sibling field added in config/fields/common.json (Integration 3 WP4).

rules.message_template: Beat "{beat_no}" could not be matched.
rules.trigger: resolveBeat() (case-insensitive exact match against ref.beats.beat_name) returns null for payload.data.beat_no. Same legacy raw-preservation side effect as local_head (beat_raw). Not scoped to the batch's target PS at all -- a beat name belonging to a different PS still resolves -- and per CLAUDE.md, 765 of 2,855 beats have no ps_id link in the official reference data at all, very likely the largest single contributor to this being the highest-volume REF_UNRESOLVED_* code in the corpus.

rules.message_template: District "{districtCell}" does not match this batch's target district ("{districtName}"). / Police Station "{psCell}" does not match this batch's target station ("{psName}").
rules.trigger: After stripping parentheticals, the words 'district'/'ps', and all punctuation, and lowercasing both sides, neither string is a substring of the other. Deliberately forgiving (substring, not exact) -- a sanity check only, never used for actual write-time scoping (P5.6); scoping is always taken from the pre-authorized batch target, never the sheet.
rules.config_driven: Hardcoded normalization regex; compares against hierarchy_nodes.name (DB data) for the batch's already-resolved target PS/district.

rules.message_template: <records.service.js validateRequiredFields's thrown message: 'Missing required fields before submit: {comma-joined field labels}'>
rules.trigger: Non-legacy imports only (isLegacy short-circuits to []): validateRequiredFields (records.service.js) -- the REAL field_registry.validation_rules.required flags, via mapper.loadRegistry, NOT the curated import-fields.config.js list and NOT the IMPORT_OPTIONAL_REQUIRED_KEYS override -- throws a 422-shaped Error listing every required-and-visible field still blank; caught here and downgraded from a hard throw to one WARNING row per composed parent. Purely advisory: DRAFT records are allowed to be incomplete (P2.4); this only previews what /records/:id/submit will eventually demand.
rules.scope: Every composed non-legacy parent row, across CASE/ARREST/KALANDRA/UIDB/MISSING/PCR_CALL
rules.config_driven: field_registry.validation_rules.required (the live DB registry) -- a DIFFERENT and stricter requiredness source than VAL-REQUIRED-FIELD uses for the same record types.

rules.message_template: No usable date found for this record (checked FIR/arrest/occurrence date fields).
rules.trigger: payload.recordDate is falsy after import.compose.js's getRecordDate() (checks fir_date/occurrence_date, date_of_arrest/arrest_date, gd_date, found_date, missing_date per record type) AND, for ARREST/KALANDRA only, the fallback to the first arrestee person row's own arrest_date also comes up empty. This is taxonomy.json's E4 (ghost/trailing row) tell -- occurs in clusters alongside REQUIRED_MISSING on truly-blank rows that PARSE-GHOST-ROW-SKIP failed to filter out (1-2 stray cells).
rules.scope: Every composed parent row, all record types
rules.config_driven: Hardcoded per-type date-field lookup order (getRecordDate, import.parse.js:312-329).

rules.message_template: FIR number "{fir_no}" already exists in the database for this Police Station.
rules.trigger: CASE record type only: the row's canonical fir_no matches (after canonicalizing BOTH the batch's candidate list and every fir_details.fir_no row for the target PS in JS -- never a SQL whereIn against canonical form, since the DB stores fir_no as raw, differently-formatted text) an FIR already in fir_details for the same ps_id. Never checked for ARREST (a repeated fir_no across arrestees on the same FIR is legitimate, and arrest_details carries no ps_id column at all).
rules.config_driven: Hardcoded query + JS-side canonicalization (findDuplicateFirsInDb); backstopped at actual write time by fir_details' real UNIQUE(ps_id, fir_year, fir_no) constraint for the remaining race window between this check and the INSERT.

rules.message_template: IO with PIS number "{io_pis}" is not registered for this police station. Register the IO first, then re-validate -- or import now and this row will be skipped.
rules.trigger: payload.data.io_pis is non-empty but its trimmed-lowercased value has no match in investigating_officers scoped to {ps_id: batchScope.psId, is_active:true} (fetched once for the whole batch, matched in JS). Deliberately ERROR in BOTH legacy and non-legacy modes -- the one ref-type lookup NOT given legacy leniency, a documented judgment call distinct from the REF_UNRESOLVED_* pattern.
rules.scope: record-level io_pis, all curated record types
rules.config_driven: investigating_officers DB table, scoped to the batch's target PS (the only ref-lookup in the whole validate stage that IS PS-scoped -- every REF_UNRESOLVED_* lookup above is global).

rules.message_template: Batch not found
rules.trigger: claimBatch(): no import_batches row for the given batchId.

rules.message_template: Only the user who uploaded the batch can confirm it
rules.trigger: batch.uploaded_by !== the confirming user's id.

rules.message_template: This batch has already been imported.
rules.trigger: batch.status === 'IMPORTED'.

rules.message_template: This batch is already being imported. Please wait for it to finish.
rules.trigger: batch.status === 'CONFIRMED' (also re-checked post-race at line 151 if the atomic UPDATE claimed 0 rows).

rules.message_template: Batch is not ready for confirmation (status must be VALIDATED, is {status})
rules.trigger: batch.status is anything other than VALIDATED (e.g. VALIDATION_PENDING, CANCELLED, FAILED).

rules.message_template: Physical temp file has expired or was removed
rules.trigger: batch.file_path is falsy or fs.existsSync(batch.file_path) is false -- the multer temp file was swept (24h startup sweep, import.router.js) or otherwise deleted before the batch was confirmed.

rules.message_template: Batch cannot be cancelled once {status} -- records may already be written.
rules.trigger: cancelBatch(): batch.status is not in ['VALIDATION_PENDING','VALIDATED'] -- append-only design, no undo once CONFIRMED/IMPORTED.

rules.message_template: Source file no longer exists -- cannot confirm
rules.trigger: processBatch(): batch.file_path is falsy or the file no longer exists on disk when the async worker actually runs (a longer gap than the claim-time check, e.g. delayed RabbitMQ redelivery after a restart). Whole batch marked FAILED (batch-level, not a per-row finding) with this clean message stored as import_batches.error_message.

rules.message_template: Uploading user account no longer exists
rules.trigger: The users row for batch.uploaded_by no longer exists at confirm time. Whole batch marked FAILED.

rules.message_template: Could not re-read the workbook at confirm time
rules.trigger: readWorkbook() returns null on the confirm-time re-read (AD7 -- confirm never trusts the validate-time in-memory object, always re-parses the source file fresh). Whole batch marked FAILED.

rules.message_template: This FIR was imported by a concurrent process between validation and confirmation.
rules.trigger: createImportedRecord() throws a Postgres error with err.code === '23505' (unique_violation) -- the fir_details UNIQUE(ps_id, fir_year, fir_no) backstop firing for a race VAL-DUPLICATE-IN-DB's fresh confirm-time re-check (moments earlier, same function) still missed (another process wrote the same FIR in between). Deliberately downgraded to WARNING with a friendly message, NOT WRITE_FAILED -- this is the ONE Postgres error code the code specifically recognizes and translates; every other DB error falls through to CONFIRM-WRITE-FAILED with the raw message intact.

rules.message_template: <raw err.message from createImportedRecord/insertRecordCore -- verbatim Postgres or JS error text, e.g. 'null value in column "record_date" of relation "records" violates not-null constraint', or a CHECK-constraint violation message>
rules.trigger: createImportedRecord() throws ANY error that is not the specifically-handled 23505 unique-violation above -- a generic catch-all. THIS IS the control-flow answer for 'why do failed rows still hit the DB': composedPayloads (the rows actually looped over here) already excludes every row invalidated by an ERROR-severity finding from THIS SAME confirm-time validateBatch re-run (invalidParentKeys filtering, whole-FIR atomicity) -- so a row with a KNOWN ERROR never reaches this INSERT attempt in the current code. WRITE_FAILED instead occurs for rows that passed every check import.validate.js actually performs, but still violate a DB constraint the validate stage never replicates -- confirmed concretely: persons.gender/persons.relation_type/record_properties.status CHECK constraints use an uppercase (or entirely different, e.g. 'INVOLVED' not existing at all) value vocabulary that field_registry's config options (Title Case: 'Male','Father','Stolen','Involved', ...) never get translated to anywhere in records.mapper.js's normalizeDetailValue/normalizePersonValue/normalizePropertyValue or records.normalize.js (grepped -- no toUpperCase/enum-map exists) -- see DB-PERSONS-GENDER-CHECK/DB-PERSONS-RELATION-TYPE-CHECK/DB-PROPERTY-STATUS-CHECK. A HISTORICAL example of this exact constraint (record_date NOT NULL) reaching an operator verbatim, alongside that same row's own ERROR-severity REQUIRED_MISSING/RECORD_DATE_MISSING findings, is preserved in backend/scripts/import-reliability/out/logs/batch-001-case.txt line 273 -- that fixture is reconstructed from a REAL pre-Integration-3 batch (its counts match db:import_batches/c13201b2... in ERROR_STATS.json exactly), i.e. from the OLD confirm code which -- per this rebuild's own stated goal (import.parse.js header comment) -- did NOT gate the INSERT on the SAME validation pass's own ERROR findings the way the current invalidParentKeys mechanism now does. Whether the current rebuilt code can still reproduce that exact co-occurrence was not re-verified by executing it (this was a read-only audit) -- flagged as a residual risk worth a live confirm-time test, not asserted as still-broken.
rules.scope: any composed record that reaches createImportedRecord
rules.config_driven: None -- generic exception passthrough; DB constraint vocabulary (CHECK lists) is fixed in migrations, field option vocabulary is fixed in config/fields/*.json, and nothing bridges the two.

rules.trigger: A batch has been CONFIRMED for more than 15 minutes with no processBatch completion (e.g. the original import.confirm.requested message never reached a handler) -- re-published on every process startup (not a recurring timer). processBatch's own leading status guard (line 257) makes this always safe/idempotent to redeliver.

rules.message_template: new row for relation "records" violates check constraint "records_record_type_check"
rules.trigger: records.record_type CHECK IN ('CASE','ARREST','PCR_CALL','MISSING','UIDB') -- 'KALANDRA' is NOT a legal value. MITIGATED: import.service.js's processBatch always writes via effectiveRecordType(batch.record_type), which maps KALANDRA -> ARREST (import.parse.js:381) before ever calling createImportedRecord, so this is not currently reachable via the import path.

rules.message_template: null value in column "record_date" of relation "records" violates not-null constraint
rules.trigger: records.record_date is NOT NULL; insertRecordCore (records.service.js) inserts recordDate directly with no fallback. MITIGATED in the current pipeline by VAL-RECORD-DATE-MISSING running at BOTH validate and confirm time and invalidating the parent before it ever reaches this INSERT -- but this is the exact constraint the historical batch-001-case.txt row-36 leak (see CONFIRM-WRITE-FAILED) violated, making it the concrete, evidenced example of what an un-mitigated gap here looks like to an operator.

rules.message_template: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "fir_details_ps_id_fir_year_fir_no_key"
rules.trigger: fir_details UNIQUE(ps_id, fir_year, fir_no) -- the backstop for VAL-DUPLICATE-IN-DB's pre-check. HANDLED, not a raw leak in practice: import.service.js specifically catches err.code === '23505' and downgrades to the friendly CONFIRM-DUPLICATE-RACE-DOWNGRADE WARNING rather than surfacing this raw message.

rules.message_template: new row for relation "record_offences" violates check constraint "record_offences_check"
rules.trigger: record_offences CHECK(act_id IS NOT NULL OR other_act_name IS NOT NULL). MITIGATED: VAL-REF-UNRESOLVED-SECTION's second trigger (import.validate.js:160-165) reproduces this exact condition (neither actId nor otherActName resolved) and invalidates the row before write, provided the row has a section but no act text. resolveAct always sets otherActName to the raw text when nothing else matches (records.normalize.js:140), so an act-only offence row with pure garbage act text should always satisfy the CHECK via the free-text fallback in practice.
rules.config_driven: Schema-only; mitigation logic lives in import.validate.js.

rules.message_template: new row for relation "persons" violates check constraint "persons_relation_type_check"
rules.trigger: persons.relation_type CHECK IN ('FATHER','MOTHER','HUSBAND','WIFE','GUARDIAN','OTHER') (uppercase). field_registry option values (config/fields/case.json:1690+, import-fields.config.js relation_type option lists) are Title Case: 'Father'/'Mother'/'Husband'/'Wife'/'Guardian'/'Other'. Same unmitigated gap and same root cause as DB-PERSONS-GENDER-CHECK -- no case-folding/enum-map step anywhere in the write path.
rules.config_driven: Same split as gender: schema CHECK vocabulary vs. field_registry option vocabulary, never reconciled.

rules.message_template: new row for relation "persons" violates check constraint "persons_gender_check"
rules.trigger: persons.gender CHECK IN ('MALE','FEMALE','OTHER','UNKNOWN') (uppercase, 4-way). field_registry option values for every gender-type field (config/fields/common.json:262+, and every curated import-fields.config.js gender list, e.g. line 62) are Title Case: 'Male'/'Female'/'Transgender'/'Unknown'. Verified by grep: neither records.mapper.js (normalizePersonValue -> coerceByType's default branch is just normalizeText, no case-folding or enum map) nor records.normalize.js contains any toUpperCase/enum-translation step for this column. 'Transgender' additionally has NO corresponding CHECK value at all (the CHECK only knows OTHER, not TRANSGENDER). UNMITIGATED -- a genuine, currently-reachable gap: ANY person row (interactive OR import) with gender='Male'/'Female'/'Transgender' will violate this CHECK at insert time and surface as CONFIRM-WRITE-FAILED with this raw message. The same gap exists in the interactive create path via the identical mapper/normalize code (out of scope of the import module itself), but the import path is where it was found during this audit and is exactly the DB_LEAK class the framework is trying to detect.
rules.scope: persons.gender -- every role/record type offering a gender SELECT field
rules.config_driven: Schema CHECK vocabulary (migration) vs. field_registry option vocabulary (config/fields/*.json + import-fields.config.js) -- the two were never reconciled; no translation layer exists anywhere in the write path.

rules.message_template: new row for relation "record_properties" violates check constraint "record_properties_status_check"
rules.trigger: record_properties.status CHECK IN ('STOLEN','RECOVERED','SEIZED','INTACT','UNCLAIMED') (uppercase, 5-way). field_registry's property_stolen_recovered/phone_status option values (config/fields/common.json:3230+, casePropertyFields/arrestPropertyFields in import-fields.config.js:207/267) are Title Case: 'Stolen'/'Recovered'/'Involved'/'Seized' -- 'Involved' has NO corresponding CHECK value AT ALL (guaranteed violation, not just a case mismatch), and the other three are case-mismatched. UNMITIGATED -- no case-folding/enum-map in records.mapper.js's normalizePropertyValue. Every property row entered as 'Involved' (a valid, offered dropdown option) is guaranteed to fail this CHECK at write time.
